resources.string: Detects when you pause on a screen so Heimdall can offer a short hint. Heimdall reads no text from other apps and never leaves the device.
An on-device co-pilot that offers a short hint when a screen stops making sense. No network, no accounts, no telemetry.

Supported: MiniCPM-V 2.6, and other vision pairs the bundled llama.cpp can run (for example Qwen3.5-VL / Bonsai). The language weights and the projector must belong together; a mismatch is rejected when picked.

Heimdall runs a vision model locally and needs two GGUF files:

1. The language weights (for MiniCPM-V 2.6: ggml-model-Q4_K_M.gguf, about 5.5 GB)
2. Its matching vision projector (for MiniCPM-V 2.6: mmproj-model-f16.gguf, about 1 GB)

Download them from openbmb/MiniCPM-V-2_6 on Hugging Face to the phone (for example Downloads), then tap “Choose file” here and pick each one. Other pairs the bundled llama.cpp supports also work when their architectures match (for example a Qwen3.5-VL language file with a qwen3vl_merger projector). Heimdall has no network permission, so the download happens in your browser, not in the app.

Your files stay where they are: the picker grants read access only. The large language weights are read straight from that grant and are never copied. The vision projector is imported once into Heimdall’s own storage (about 1 GB) because llama.cpp needs a normal file path for it; it is kept until you pick a different projector, and you can free it by clearing the app’s storage.

A GGUF whose architecture, projector type or tensor packing is unsupported, or a weights/projector pair from different model families, is rejected when picked instead of failing halfway through loading. Tap “Test pair” to have llama.cpp load the selection once and report whether it really works on this device — the file checks can only predict, the runtime verdict is the real one.

Files packed in a private format that needs the PrismML binaries (PQ2_0 or PTQ1_0 tensor types, or an -MTP- drafter head) cannot be read by the bundled llama.cpp; use the Q2_0 or a standard quantisation instead.

Cloud-only documents cannot be used because they must be read as local files.

Android 13+ blocks this toggle for sideloaded apps. Open the main App info page (not the Permissions page), tap ⋮ and choose “Allow restricted settings”, then enable the gesture observer. If that menu item is missing on your build, copy the ADB commands below and run them from a PC or Termux. Heimdall still works without this service: it then notices a pause from screen changes instead.
